messages:
anya_support: Hey team, escalation from Acme Payments — their Console streaming chart for TTFT and tokens/sec is showing missing datapoints and sometimes negative values since 02:00 UTC. They're seeing this on /streams route only. Customer said it started after last night's deploy.

miguel_eng: Thanks, anya. Do we have the session IDs or a repro?

anya_support: Pasting the session id and a sanitized request: session=acme-79b1; request:
```
POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{"model":"redwood-medium","input":"hello","stream":true}
```
They attached a screenshot showing -12.3 tokens/sec on the chart.

lina_sre: metrics-bot, can you dump the raw TTFT and token counters for that org and time window (1711996800-1712004000)?

metrics-bot: raw_metrics: org=acme-payments, route=/v1/streams, metric=streaming.tokens_emitted, window=1m, sample: [ 0, 45, 62, -12, 58 ]
Note: negative at 02:13:00 UTC.

miguel_eng: Negative tokens emitted is impossible at emitter level. Could be a subtraction of cumulative counters that reset. Suspect rollover or a counter reset combined with out-of-order ingestion. Any recent changes to the telemetry pipeline?

samir_product: We did flip a telemetry feature-flag last night that switches ingestion to kafka-topic-v2 for streams. Rollout was gradual but target was 02:00 UTC.

lina_sre: That lines up. If cumulative counter reset and we compute rate as delta/t where we don't handle negative delta, you'll get negative rate. Quick repro: if counter goes from 1000 -> 5 (reset) and window is 1s, rate=(5-1000)/1 = -995. Need to gate negative deltas.

miguel_eng: Agreed. I'll check the aggregation service. Adding a quick guard to ignore deltas < 0 and treat as reset. Deploying a patch to metrics-aggregator canary now. @deploy-bot can you kick canary for metrics-aggregator?

deploy-bot: Canary started: metrics-aggregator@canary-20260317-1. Rolling to 10% traffic.

anya_support: Customer is asking for ETA for a fix and whether their billing is affected by the negative tokens/sec. They saw spikes and a single billing anomaly ticket.

miguel_eng: Fix should be within 30m to canary, 90m for full roll if canary healthy. Billing: negative display only — billing uses authoritative token counters from backend accounting service (different pipeline). I'll confirm with finance, but I don't expect actual charge changes.

lina_sre: Added alert to watch for any other negative deltas across services and backfilled last 24h to find any other orgs. Found 3 other orgs with transient negative values between 01:50-02:30 UTC.

samir_product: I'll notify affected customers and mark incident as "dashboard-metrics-display" — low severity but visible. Any need for a postmortem?

miguel_eng: Yes, after closure. Root cause: telemetry ingestion switch + not handling counter resets. Action items: 1) patch aggregator to ignore negative deltas and emit reset event (miguel). 2) add unit tests and e2e for counter rollover (miguel). 3) notify billing team to confirm no charge impact (anya). 4) update rollout checklist to include telemetry smoke tests (samir).

anya_support: Sending interim note to Acme: "We believe this is a display issue caused by telemetry pipeline migration. Engineers are rolling a fix; expected resolution within 90 minutes. Billing unaffected pending confirmation." :thumbsup:

metrics-bot: Canary health: OK at 10% for 8m. No new negative deltas reported for acme-payments.

miguel_eng: Canary looks good, promoting to stable. Deploying stable now.

deploy-bot: Deploy successful: metrics-aggregator@stable-20260317-3.

lina_sre: Confirmed display corrected for acme-payments backfill to current time. Closing thread after billing confirmation.

anya_support: Billing team confirmed no charge changes. Closing the escalation, customer updated. :white_check_mark:

samir_product: I'll draft a short postmortem and ship the telemetry smoke test to rollout checklist.

anya_support: Thanks everyone!
